analyst_view.overall: Early view: Barcelona (5th, 9 points) arrive in strong form after beating Aston Villa 3-0 and Atletico Madrid 2-1 to lead LaLiga, but Lamine Yamal has a knee problem that ruled him out of Spain's next game and Rodri has a hamstring injury. Sabah (31st, 3 points) lost 4-1 at Viking and are without Aden McCarthy, sent off in that game (ban not yet served). The long trip to Baku and a busy league schedule make some Barcelona rotation likely.

goals.text: The numbers say 5.2 goals, which looks too high. Barcelona should win comfortably, but with Yamal's knee a doubt and Hansi Flick possibly resting players for the long trip east, a 3-0 or 4-0 looks more likely than a five-goal rout. Sabah did score at Viking, so a consolation goal is possible.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and I lean slightly higher. Barcelona will camp in Sabah's half and the hosts will defend deep, which is how corners build up. Even a rotated Barcelona side keeps the ball for long spells.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Sabah had two players booked and one sent off at Viking, so tired defending late in the game could add bookings. Barcelona usually pick up few cards in one-sided games. I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.8 shots and I stay with it. Even without Yamal, Barcelona have Raphinha in form (two goals against Villa) and Fermin Lopez fresh from a brace at Atletico, so the shot count will be high. Sabah should manage few attempts of their own.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.5 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Rotation and Yamal's knee injury could take some sharpness out of the attack, and a comfortable lead often slows the second half. I expect a total closer to ten or eleven.
